newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling in fitter form after shakeout.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling in fitter form after shakeout.

text.p: Sterling is in fitter shape after Friday's shakeout, and despite a slight slip in early Europe should soon return to the upside, chartists said.

"The sell-off we've seen would have caught most of the longs that weren't secure, so it's really just cleaned the market out. I think we could see it stay strong and perhaps even go higher," said Ian Park, director at Capital Management in Zurich.
Sterling/mark should hold 2.7850 with a view to breaking 2.81 for levels as high as 2.84 farther out, Park said.
The pound was quoted at 2.7985/95 marks at 0836 GMT, down from late Friday's European level of 2.8052.
Ivo Pescia, customer adviser at Olsen and Associates in Zurich, plotted near-term support around 2.7950 marks, with 2.7910 below there.
"For today I think we can see it slightly higher, back to 2.8080, and by the end of the week it should be able to go to 2.8350," Pescia said.
In the short term, however, the 2.8250 area -- just above sterling's recent 4-1/2-year high -- should cap, chartists said.
Against the dollar, the pound's early dip beneath $1.62 will encounter healthy support at $1.6150 -- a site of previous congestion -- which should hold for now, analysts predicted.
Stefan Steinemann, technical analyst at Lloyds Bank in Geneva, said that prop should hold for now, but there was scope for a deeper dip to $1.60 or even $1.59 in the medium term.
That, however, should contain the downside and reinstall sterling in its uptrend, he said.
Analysts noted early resistance around $1.6300, where a down trendline drawn from the April 1 peak of $1.6370 cuts in.
The pound stood at $1.6205/11 at 0950 GMT versus its previous European close here of $1.6220.
RSI - 14 day: Sterling/mark: 55 pct, sterling/dollar: 46 pct
